messages:
Anika S.: quick thread: after the RFC, ops asked about a 'precision seam' that can switch precision inside a single forward pass without breaking determinism or cacheability. thoughts?

Dev P.: primary engineering risks i see: kernel selection churn (lots of small launches), kv format mismatch, and nondeterministic fp rounding across switches.

Noah K.: from perf runs: two practical modes worked: 1) layer-granular switch (change precision at layer boundaries) and 2) block-granular (every 32/64 tokens). layer-granular has lower kernel overhead but is coarser.

Anika S.: good. requirement: client replay must produce identical tokens if given identical seed + inputs + precision_policy. we need precise contract.

Dev P.: propose API: add precision_seam {"mode":"layer|block|none","grace_tokens":4} inside quant_profile. default none. runtime emits trace event when seam occurs.

Noah K.: sample request we tested:
```json
{
  "model": "rwd-7b",
  "quant_profile": "cost-savings-v2",
  "precision_seam": {"mode": "block", "block_size": 32}
}
```

Anika S.: nice. about KV: storing separate kv per precision explodes memory. we should canonicalize to FP16 and cache that. at switch time, lazily cast slice to target precision on GPU. saves memory and keeps single cache key.

Dev P.: lazy-cast tradeoffs: extra cast latency and extra memory bandwidth during switch. we measured ~0.3-0.6ms per layer on A100 for 2048 sequences. batching casts helps. also need to ensure casts are bit-compatible across drivers.

Noah K.: another subtlety: rotary/rope and alibi-style positional transforms sometimes rely on scale behaviour; casting can shift numeric ranges and cause small drift. QA-team: add positional-encoding test vectors in the matrix.

QA-team: noted. will add small corpus to catch degenerate edge cases (replay, long-range attention, rope/rotary stress).

infra-bot: FYI: canary pool request template created. Please add estimated qps and duration. :information_source:

Anika S.: also security/compliance note: if we allow per-request precision, audit logs must include precision transitions and final precision map for the response. this helps incident repro and customer queries.

Dev P.: telemetry fields suggested: endpoint, model, profile, seam_mode, switch_points (list), pre_metrics (entropy,kvl2), post_metrics, latency_penalty_ms. keep names stable.

Noah K.: fallback behavior: if cast fails or kernel missing fallback to endpoint-level default (no seam) and mark as degraded in telemetry. Runtime should expose a boolean in response metadata: precision_seam_applied=true/false.

Anika S.: rollout plan: 1) internal canary only; 2) run 2-week A/B with 5% traffic; 3) collect quality deltas using eval harness (same prompts, compare nll+human spot checks); 4) if stable, expose opt-in flag to customers.

Dev P.: open implementation questions: do we need a new compilation artifact for each precision variant or can we reuse kernel caches with runtime casts? re-compilation per-variant is heavy. prefer reuse + cast.

Noah K.: agreed. heavy recompile hurts startup. reuse kernels and implement tiny shim that casts KV and selects the per-layer kernel where available. keep a simple policy for when exact kernel missing: run in next higher-precision supported.

Anika S.: action items: - Dev + Noah: benchmark lazy-cast overhead for longctx (8k, 32k) and different batch sizes by Tue EOD. - QA-team: add positional encoding tests and replay checks by next Wed. - Dev: draft the API contract + telemetry fields and submit short RFC follow-up.

infra-bot: scheduled: canary-pool request submitted to eng-sre (id: CP-2026-11).

Noah K.: one last note: for models using grouped attention optimizations we should verify that group boundaries align with seam boundaries to avoid partial-group precision mismatches. adding to checklist.

Anika S.: thanks all. we'll sync in next eng-ml sync if benchmarks look promising. :thumbsup:
